newsitem.title: ITALY: Eni suggests Egypt-Turkey gas pipeline.
newsitem.headline: Eni suggests Egypt-Turkey gas pipeline.

text.p: Italian energy group Eni said it will invest $2 billion in a new underwater gas pipeline between Egypt and Turkey, if original plans to build a line between Egypt and Israel fall through.
Eni chairman Guglielmo Moscato told a Middle East economic conference in Cairo that the alternative plan would not be as cost-effective as the so-called peace pipeline.

"The peace pipeline remains the best solution both in terms of economics and politics," Eni quoted Moscato as saying on Tuesday. Eni was set to invest $1.4 billion in the Egypt-Israel link, but the project has been blocked since the installation of the new government in Israel, Moscato added.

The new project would involve laying a gas line along the Mediterranean sea bed between Egypt's Port Said and Turkey's Iskenderun and Antalya. The pipeline would have to carry at least 10 billion cubic metres of gas a year, Eni said.
"We cannot lose time. Other operators are already moving. Russia has reached a deal with Turkey," Eni managing director Franco Bernabe was quoted as saying.
"Either one has to protect one's market position or else one is thrown out." -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
